items.subject: Import AI 471: Why Hugging Face worries me; space mining; Five Eyes on AI
items.rationale: Two direct-scope threads in one issue. (1) 'Why Hugging Face worries me' — Jack Clark's take on Hugging Face lines up with the existing entities/hugging-face page (recent NVIDIA $13B acquisition Aug 27, July 2026 OpenAI agent breach, open-weight distribution rail). High-value first-party commentary on an already-tracked entity. (2) 'Five Eyes on AI' — intelligence-alliance AI governance maps to concepts/ai-policy and concepts/ai-governance-political-pressure. Import AI is a high-signal tracked source; 'space mining' item is out of scope.
items.caveat: importai substack slug inferred from open.substack.com/pub/importai link — verify canonical URL before scrape; typically free-access

items.subject: [AINews] Fal's H3 Max Live breaks the infinite videogen barrier
items.rationale: Fal 'H3 Max Live' is a real-time/infinite video-generation model release — directly feeds the actively-maintained concepts/ai-video-generation-2026 page. Video gen is adjacent to core LLM/agent scope but the existing page shows the wiki tracks this line. The AINews digest form is a broad daily roundup (20 redirect links) — downstream scrape should extract the lead videogen item and skip noise.
items.caveat: ainews digest aggregates many links; scrape should focus on the videogen lead, not the whole roundup. smol.ai substack may be free-access.

items.subject: 🎙️ How I AI: How this PM uses Claude to handle 70% to 80% of his workday
items.source: Lenny's Newsletter (substack publication_id=10845, @lenny) — 'How I AI' podcast/workflow post
items.rationale: Concrete Claude usage workflow (PM offloading 70-80% of workday) is practical material for the Claude Code best-practices / steering-methods and AI-workflow concept pages. Lenny is a tracked entity. Applied-agent-usage angle is squarely in wiki scope.
items.caveat: 'How I AI' is podcast-led; text transcript availability unconfirmed before ingest — may need YouTube/podcast fallback.

items.subject: Korea Just Made AI a Public Utility, Free for Everyone
items.source: beehiiv newsletter (all links are link.mail.beehiiv.com click-tracking wrappers)
items.rationale: A national AI-as-public-utility policy move is a strong signal for concepts/korean-ai and concepts/ai-policy (sovereign/public AI infrastructure trend). Kept at medium because it is policy/industry news rather than core LLM/agent tech, and every link is an opaque beehiiv redirect wrapper — no canonical URL recoverable from the checkpoint, so scrape requires redirect resolution first.
items.caveat: beehiiv redirect links only; resolve redirect to get canonical URL before scrape

items.subject: Exclusive Early Access: Final 3 Chapters of The Hundred-Page Deep Reinforcement Learning Book
items.rationale: Promotional/marketing email for a paid RL book early-access offer (Link 10 is an explicit paywall/coupon redirect). No novel technical content, no release or research contribution. Out of core LLM/agent wiki scope; skip unless a reinforcement-learning concept page is being seeded, in which case a source is the book itself, not this ad.
items.caveat: paywalled promotional content; not worth scraping

notes: All five digests are single-post Substack/beehiiv emails: the ~19-20 'articles' per digest are Substack chrome (post-title, like/comment/share, read-in-app, subscribe-widget) plus tokenized /redirect/ links, not distinct articles.
Canonical URLs were inferred from open.substack.com/pub/<handle>/p/<slug> links in the digests, not scraped. Verify before ingest.

Notable batch themes: (1) Hugging Face governance concern (Import AI) lands right after the tracked NVIDIA $13B acquisition — worth a same-day entities/hugging-face touch; (2) a real-time videogen model release (Fal H3 Max Live) continues the ai-video-generation-2026 thread; (3) sovereign/public AI infrastructure (Korea utility policy) is an emerging ai-policy sub-theme.
Korea and DataCamp-style beehiiv posts have no recoverable canonical URL from the checkpoint — downstream must resolve click-tracking redirects before scraping.
Downstream stage (newsletter-wiki-ingest) should read this file, not the raw checkpoint.
